shared.concept_anchor: Danashtuti hymns and patron-priest relationship in Rigveda

en.display_text:
With reference to the role of gift-giving and priestly power in the Vedic religious economy, consider the following statements:

1. Danashtuti hymns in the Rigveda are praise compositions celebrating the generosity of wealthy patrons who sponsored sacrificial rituals, providing evidence for the patron-priest economic relationship in Early Vedic society.
2. The shift from simple fire oblations in the Early Vedic period to elaborate, costly sacrificial rituals in the Later Vedic period was primarily motivated by a desire to reduce the economic influence of the Brahmin priestly class.
3. Dana (charitable giving) served a political function in the Vedic polity by linking a ruler's generosity to his religious legitimacy and social authority.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 2 and 3 only
(b) 1 and 3 only
(c) 1 and 2 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Danashtuti hymns in the Rigveda are praise compositions celebrating the generosity of wealthy patrons who sponsored sacrificial rituals, providing evidence for the patron-priest economic relationship in Early Vedic society.
statement_analysis.reason: Danashtuti (Dana + Stuti = praise of gifts) hymns are a recognised category in Rigvedic scholarship — they celebrate patrons' generosity (cattle, gold, etc.) and are evidence for the economic basis of early priestly patronage.

statement_analysis.statement: The shift from simple fire oblations in the Early Vedic period to elaborate, costly sacrificial rituals in the Later Vedic period was primarily motivated by a desire to reduce the economic influence of the Brahmin priestly class.
statement_analysis.reason: The opposite is true — the shift to elaborate ritual INCREASED Brahmin economic and social power, as only they possessed the specialist knowledge required for complex Shrauta sacrifices. The elaboration of ritual was a mechanism of Brahmin ascendancy, not a check on it.

statement_analysis.statement: Dana (charitable giving) served a political function in the Vedic polity by linking a ruler's generosity to his religious legitimacy and social authority.
statement_analysis.reason: Dana's political dimension is well-attested in Vedic sources — generous gift-giving (particularly at sacrifices) created networks of obligation and demonstrated the ruler's ability to command and distribute surplus, directly tied to political legitimacy.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) is a strong distractor because all three statements sound plausible in isolation — students who skim Statement 2 without noticing the reversed causation will accept all three as correct.
elimination_logic: Statement 1: Danashtuti as praise hymns for generous patrons is a factual category in Rigvedic scholarship — Statement 1 is correct.
Statement 2: The claim that ritual elaboration aimed to REDUCE Brahmin influence is a reversed-causation error — elaboration INCREASED Brahmin power and monopoly. Statement 2 is incorrect.
Statement 3: Dana's link to political legitimacy is well-established in Vedic polity analysis — Statement 3 is correct.
Statements 1 and 3 correct, Statement 2 incorrect — answer is option (b): 1 and 3 only.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 2 uses a reversed-causation partial-truth structure. The facts embedded in it are real: there was a shift from simple to elaborate ritual, and the Brahmin class was economically powerful. But the causal direction is inverted — elaborate ritual was the mechanism of Brahmin ascendancy, not a constraint on it. Students who read quickly and accept the factual premises without checking the causal claim will mark Statement 2 correct.
en.final_explanation:
The Vedic economy of religious exchange involved both transactional priest-fees (Dakshina) and broader gift-giving (Dana), each with distinct social functions.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Danashtuti hymns are an important evidence base for understanding Early Vedic patronage economics. They record gifts of cattle, horses, and gold, giving historians a window into resource distribution.
• Statement 2 — Incorrect: The elaboration of Shrauta ritual in the Later Vedic period was a vehicle for expanding Brahmin power — not limiting it. Only Brahmins had the esoteric knowledge to perform complex multi-day sacrifices. This created dependency and justified both priestly fees (Dakshina) and social status.
• Statement 3 — Correct: Dana functioned as a form of soft political power in Vedic polity — the ability to give lavishly demonstrated a king's divine favour and surplus command, legitimising his authority.

Value Addition:
• The distinction between Dana (general giving) and Dakshina (specific priest fee) is a UPSC-tested precision point.
• Brahmin claims to 'Brahmanatva' (the quality of being Brahmin) were justified through their monopoly on ritual knowledge — economic power followed from knowledge monopoly.
• The Later Vedic Brahmana texts themselves are the product of and justification for this priestly ascendancy.

वैदिक धार्मिक अर्थव्यवस्था में दान और पुरोहित शक्ति की भूमिका के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

shared.concept_anchor: Soma — dual identity as deity and ritual substance, Book IX

en.display_text:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) about the Soma cult in Vedic religion:

Assertion (A): The entire ninth Mandala (Book IX) of the Rigveda is exclusively dedicated to Soma, making it the only deity in the Rigveda to receive a complete, dedicated book of hymns.

Reason (R): Soma occupies a unique position in Vedic religion as both a venerated deity addressed in prayer and the central ritual substance physically consumed by priests during Shrauta sacrifices — a dual identity found in no other major Vedic deity.

(a) Both A and R are correct, and R is the correct explanation of A
(b) Both A and R are correct, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
(c) A is correct but R is incorrect
(d) A is incorrect but R is correct
en.strong_distractor: b — Option (b) is a strong distractor because students who accept both A and R as correct but doubt whether 'Soma's role as a ritual drink' explains 'entire Book IX being dedicated to Soma' may choose (b), not recognising that the dual role IS the causal explanation for the dedicated Mandala.
elimination_logic: Step 1: Is Assertion (A) correct? — The entire ninth Mandala (Book IX) of the Rigveda is indeed dedicated to Soma. Yes, A is correct.
Step 2: Is Reason (R) correct? — Soma is indeed unique in simultaneously being a venerated deity AND the central ritual substance consumed in Shrauta sacrifices. Yes, R is correct.

Step 3: Does R causally explain A? — Yes. The reason an entire book is devoted to Soma is precisely this dual identity — Soma must be simultaneously hymned (as a god) and used (as a drink) within the same ritual context, requiring a dedicated corpus of hymns that serve both invocatory and procedural functions. R explains A.
Both A and R correct AND R explains A — correct option is (a).
en.final_explanation:
Soma's unique position in Vedic religion — being both the deity addressed and the substance consumed — explains why it warranted an entire dedicated Mandala in the Rigveda.

Assertion (A): The ninth Mandala of the Rigveda (Soma Mandala) is exclusively dedicated to Soma. This is correct and unambiguous.

Reason (R): Soma is unique in the Vedic pantheon for its dual identity — it is simultaneously a deity who must be invoked and praised, and a physical ritual substance (pressed plant juice) that is consumed during the sacrifice. This dual identity is correct.

R explains A: The reason Book IX is devoted entirely to Soma is that this dual role required a substantial, dedicated hymn corpus. Unlike Indra (who is praised but not physically consumed) or Agni (who is the fire, not a drink), Soma's simultaneous status as both divine and physical — as both subject of worship and object of ritual consumption — demanded an integrated body of hymns addressing both dimensions.

Value Addition:
• The soma-pressing ritual (using stones to extract the juice) was itself a sacred act with precise procedural rules.
• The Soma Mandala's hymns are primarily in the Gayatri metre — they tend to be shorter and more repetitive than other Rigvedic hymns.
• The Avestan Haoma and the Vedic Soma share etymology and ritual function — evidence of shared Indo-Iranian religious heritage predating the separation of the two branches.

hi.display_text:
वैदिक धर्म में सोम उपासना के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथन (A) और कारण (R) पर विचार करें:

कथन (A): ऋग्वेद का पूरा नवां मंडल (पुस्तक IX) विशेष रूप से सोम को समर्पित है, जो इसे ऋग्वेद में एकमात्र ऐसा देवता बनाता है जिसे पूर्ण, समर्पित स्तोत्रों की एक पूरी पुस्तक प्राप्त है।

कारण (R): सोम वैदिक धर्म में एक अनूठा स्थान रखता है क्योंकि यह एक पूजनीय देवता है जिसे प्रार्थना में संबोधित किया जाता है और साथ ही श्रौत यज्ञों के दौरान पुरोहितों द्वारा भौतिक रूप से ग्रहण किया जाने वाला केंद्रीय अनुष्ठानिक पदार्थ भी है — यह द्वैध पहचान किसी अन्य प्रमुख वैदिक देवता में नहीं पाई जाती।

(a) A और R दोनों सही हैं, और R, A की सही व्याख्या है
(b) A और R दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं है
(c) A सही है लेकिन R गलत है
(d) A गलत है लेकिन R सही है
hi.strong_distractor: b — विकल्प (b) एक मजबूत भ्रमकारी है क्योंकि छात्र जो A और R दोनों को सही मानते हैं लेकिन संदेह करते हैं कि 'सोम की भूमिका एक अनुष्ठानिक पेय के रूप में' 'पूरी पुस्तक IX को सोम को समर्पित किए जाने' की व्याख्या करती है या नहीं, वे (b) चुन सकते हैं, यह न समझते हुए कि द्वैध भूमिका ही समर्पित मंडल के लिए कारणात्मक व्याख्या है।
elimination_logic: चरण 1: क्या कथन (A) सही है? — ऋग्वेद का पूरा नवां मंडल (पुस्तक IX) वास्तव में सोम को समर्पित है। हाँ, A सही है।
चरण 2: क्या कारण (R) सही है? — सोम वास्तव में एक अनूठा देवता है जो एक साथ पूजनीय देवता और श्रौत यज्ञों में प्रयुक्त केंद्रीय अनुष्ठानिक पदार्थ दोनों है। हाँ, R सही है।

चरण 3: क्या R, A की कारणात्मक व्याख्या करता है? — हाँ। एक पूरी पुस्तक सोम को समर्पित होने का कारण यही द्वैध पहचान है — सोम को एक देवता के रूप में स्तुत किया जाना और एक पेय के रूप में उपयोग किया जाना आवश्यक है, जिसके लिए ऐसे स्तोत्रों का समर्पित संग्रह चाहिए जो आवाहन और अनुष्ठान दोनों कार्यों को पूरा करें। R, A को समझाता है।
A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A को समझाता है — सही विकल्प (a) है।
hi.final_explanation:
सोम की वैदिक धर्म में अनूठी स्थिति — जो एक ओर देवता है जिसे संबोधित किया जाता है और दूसरी ओर वह पदार्थ है जिसे ग्रहण किया जाता है — यह समझाती है कि ऋग्वेद में इसे एक पूरा समर्पित मंडल क्यों मिला।

कथन (A): ऋग्वेद का नवां मंडल (सोम मंडल) विशेष रूप से सोम को समर्पित है। यह सही और स्पष्ट है।

कारण (R): वैदिक देवताओं में सोम की द्वैध पहचान अनूठी है — यह एक ओर देवता है जिसे आवाहन और स्तुति की जाती है, और दूसरी ओर एक भौतिक अनुष्ठानिक पदार्थ (दबाया हुआ पौधों का रस) है जिसे यज्ञ के दौरान ग्रहण किया जाता है। यह द्वैध पहचान सही है।

R, A को समझाता है: पुस्तक IX पूरी तरह से सोम को समर्पित है क्योंकि इस द्वैध भूमिका के लिए एक समर्पित स्तोत्र संग्रह आवश्यक था। इंद्र (जिसे स्तुत किया जाता है लेकिन ग्रहण नहीं किया जाता) या अग्नि (जो अग्नि है, पेय नहीं) के विपरीत, सोम की देवता और भौतिक दोनों स्थिति के कारण एक समेकित स्तोत्र संग्रह की आवश्यकता थी जो दोनों आयामों को संबोधित करता हो।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• सोम रस निकालने की अनुष्ठानिक प्रक्रिया (पत्थरों से रस निकालना) स्वयं एक पवित्र क्रिया थी जिसमें सटीक नियम थे।
• सोम मंडल के स्तोत्र मुख्यतः गायत्री छंद में हैं — ये अन्य ऋग्वैदिक स्तोत्रों की तुलना में छोटे और अधिक पुनरावृत्तिपूर्ण होते हैं।
• अवेस्ता का होमा और वैदिक सोम समान व्युत्पत्ति और अनुष्ठानिक कार्य साझा करते हैं — यह दोनों शाखाओं के विभाजन से पूर्व के साझा इंडो-ईरानी धार्मिक विरासत का प्रमाण है।

en.display_text:
Which of the following represents the correct sequence of major ceremonial acts within a Vedic Shrauta Soma sacrifice?

I.   The Hotri priest recites invocatory hymns from the Rigveda, summoning the deities to be present at the sacrifice
II.  The pressed Soma juice is poured as an oblation into the Ahavaniya fire as the culminating sacrificial act
III. The Soma plant is physically pressed to extract its juice while the Udgatri chants Sama songs
IV.  The three sacred fires — Garhapatya, Ahavaniya, and Dakshina — are established and consecrated at the sacrificial site

(a) I → IV → III → II
(b) IV → I → III → II
(c) IV → III → I → II
(d) I → III → IV → II
en.strong_distractor: c — Option (c) is a strong distractor because it correctly places the preparatory fire-lighting before Soma pressing but reverses the sequence of invocatory hymns and actual Soma offering, exploiting students who know the broad sequence but not the precise order.
elimination_logic: In a Shrauta Soma sacrifice, the logical-ritual sequence begins with establishing the sacred fires — Garhapatya, Ahavaniya, and Dakshina — as the foundation of the sacred space.
Once fires are established, the Hotri priest recites invocatory Rigvedic hymns to summon and welcome the deities — this must happen before the actual offering.
The Soma pressing follows the invocatory hymns — the plant is pressed to extract juice while the Udgatri chants Sama songs.
The actual pouring of pressed Soma juice as oblation into the Ahavaniya fire is the culminating act — following pressing and chanting. Correct sequence: IV → I → III → II → option (b).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The temporal-swap trap targets the order of invocation versus Soma pressing — students who know both happen before the final offering may reverse their internal sequence. Option (c) places Soma pressing before invocatory hymns, which is the wrong order — invocations welcome the deity first, then the substance is prepared and offered. The Hotri's recitation (invoking deities) precedes the Adhvaryu/Udgatri's Soma processing activities.
en.final_explanation:
The Shrauta Soma sacrifice follows a precise ritual sequence — each step has a theological rationale for its position.

Correct sequence: IV → I → III → II

• IV (Establishment of three sacred fires): First, Garhapatya, Ahavaniya, and Dakshina fires are kindled and consecrated — these define and sanctify the sacrificial ground. Nothing else can proceed without this.
• I (Hotri recites invocatory Rigvedic hymns): The Hotri summons the gods and invites them to the sacrifice — deities must be invited before they can receive offerings.
• III (Pressing of Soma plant and Udgatri's Sama-chanting): The Soma plant is pressed to extract juice while Sama songs are chanted — the substance of the offering is prepared.
• II (Soma juice poured as oblation into the Ahavaniya fire): The culminating act — the prepared Soma is offered to the fire as the deities receive their share.

Wrong options reverse the pressing/invocation order or misplace fire establishment.

Value Addition:
• The Agnishtoma is the simplest complete Soma sacrifice — understanding its sequence gives the template for all more elaborate Soma sacrifices.
• The Adhvaryu priest manages the physical mechanics of soma pressing and fire maintenance throughout the sequence.
• The Brahman priest's supervisory role spans all four stages — he monitors for errors at every step.

श्रौत सोम यज्ञ एक सटीक आचारिक क्रम का पालन करता है — प्रत्येक चरण की अपनी धार्मिक तर्कसंगतता होती है।

सही क्रम: IV → I → III → II

• IV (तीन पवित्र अग्नियों की स्थापना): पहले गर्हपत्य, आहवनिय, और दक्षिणा अग्नि प्रज्वलित और अभिषिक्त की जाती हैं — ये यज्ञ स्थल को परिभाषित और पवित्र करती हैं। इसके बिना आगे कुछ भी संभव नहीं।
• I (होत्री ऋग्वैदिक आह्वानात्मक मंत्रों का पाठ करता है): होत्री देवताओं को बुलाता है और यज्ञ में आमंत्रित करता है — देवताओं को अर्पण प्राप्त करने से पहले आमंत्रित करना आवश्यक है।
• III (सोम पौधे को दबाना और उद्गात्रि का साम गायन): सोम पौधे को रस निकालने के लिए दबाया जाता है जबकि साम गीत गाए जाते हैं — अर्पण की सामग्री तैयार होती है।
• II (सोम रस को आहवनिय अग्नि में अर्पण के रूप में डाला जाता है): अंतिम क्रिया — तैयार सोम अग्नि को अर्पित किया जाता है क्योंकि देवता अपना हिस्सा प्राप्त करते हैं।

गलत विकल्प दबाने/आह्वान क्रम को उलट देते हैं या अग्नि स्थापना को गलत स्थान देते हैं।

मूल्य संवर्धन:
• अग्निष्टोम सबसे सरल पूर्ण सोम यज्ञ है — इसके क्रम को समझना सभी जटिल सोम यज्ञों के लिए आधार देता है।
• अध्वर्यु पुरोहित पूरे क्रम में सोम दबाने और अग्नि रखरखाव की भौतिक क्रियाओं का प्रबंधन करता है।
• ब्राह्मण पुरोहित की पर्यवेक्षी भूमिका चारों चरणों में होती है — वह हर चरण में त्रुटियों की निगरानी करता है।
